# Divergences from the original

<!-- generated by tools/faithfulness/registers.py; do not edit by hand -->

Every place where the C# deliberately behaves differently from the original, collected from the
`// DIVERGENCE:` comments in `src/`. Each entry names where it is in the C# (file:line,
type.member), the original function(s) (by coordinate) from the nearest `// orig:` comment above it, and the
reason given in the comment (`why`). The class is derived by `tools/faithfulness/registers.py`
(a keyword heuristic, corrected by `tools/faithfulness/overrides.csv`):

| Class | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `undefined-memory` | the original reads or writes outside its defined data: garbage, out of bounds, uninitialised variables, stack leftovers, stale globals, a null far pointer |
| `host` | input/output, timing, rendering, audio, files, DOS/EMS, the clock |
| `not-modelled` | a feature or state that is not implemented yet (or is done by another layer) |
| `deliberate-fix` | the original would hang or crash, or has a defect, and the C# does not |
| `other` | a representation difference or anything else |

Core logic (rules, cards, events, travel, battles, persistence) comes first; presentation and
host entries follow. The `not-modelled`, `deliberate-fix` and `other` entries of the core logic,
and the `undefined-memory` ones, are reviewed in [DIVERGENCE_REVIEW.md](DIVERGENCE_REVIEW.md).
`divergences.csv` holds the same data for filtering. Entry ids are stable (a hash of the file and
the start of the note); do not edit this file, edit the comments and regenerate with
`python tools/faithfulness/registers.py`.

#### deliberate-fix (7)

- **D-2a45ce** `deliberate-fix` - `src/Darklands.Core/Items/ItemStores.cs:82` `ItemStores.CanPut`  
  original: `R035+0x1350` (1462:1350, matched)  
  why: with OriginalBehaviour.FixCacheStoreLimit (or FixInnCacheRewrite) the original's Put never refuses; here a Put that would need a 63rd live store or a 128th entry of a store is refused when it is made (cache_key, R035 keys 0x1950/0x1970), the item staying in the member's pack, so that closing the screen cannot lose items.
- **D-fefefc** `deliberate-fix` - `src/Darklands.Core/Items/ItemStores.cs:99` `ItemStores.CanPut`  
  original: `R035+0x1350` (1462:1350, matched)  
  why: data safety (FixCacheStoreLimit): a new entry or store that no layout of the live stores can hold within 16-bit offsets and a file of at most 0xFFFF bytes is refused too (the file is then only ever written in place, see CloseCompact), the item staying in the pack.
- **D-856386** `deliberate-fix` - `src/Darklands.Core/Items/ItemStores.cs:169` `ItemStores.CloseCompact`  
  original: `R035+0x04BC` (1462:04BC, matched), `R035+0x1468` (1462:1468, matched)  
  why: with OriginalBehaviour.FixInnCacheRewrite or FixCacheStoreLimit (data safety, switchable; on in the player's game) the append and the rewrite of a known store (cache_save R035+0x1468) are not made: the stores the places refer to are read by their offsets and the file is laid out compactly, the way the original's own cache_save reads and rewrites it without loss: byte 0 = 124, byte 1 the store count, the offsets from 2 (store h at 2h), store 1 at 126, the stores packed in handle order and nothing after the last. At most 62 stores, 127 entries a store; stores no place refers to are dropped and the places' handles (Location +0x18) renumbered. The original lays out a 198-byte table, whose rewrite loses stores (cbw R035+0x1615), and has no limit (the append at R035+0x1532). Put is refused beyond the limits (CanPut). A file the original itself wrote can already hold more than 62 live stores or a store of more than 127 entries: closing in it never fails and loses nothing; the stores are laid out in a table large enough for them (the original's 198-byte one, or byte 0 = half the table with 2 bytes a store), a file beyond what the original's own rewrite handles, as its own files are. A file whose stores cannot be laid out within 16-bit offsets and 0xFFFF bytes at all is never laid out again, see WriteInPlace. A place's handle that names no store (not -1, past the file's count) has nothing to drop: only the handle is reset to -1, which reads an empty store just as the invalid one does.
- **D-02cb31** `deliberate-fix` - `src/Darklands.Core/Items/ItemStores.cs:217` `ItemStores.WriteInPlace`  
  original: `R035+0x04BC` (1462:04BC, matched), `R035+0x1468` (1462:1468, matched)  
  why: data safety (FixCacheStoreLimit): when no layout keeps every store offset and the file size within 16 bits (a file of at most 0xFFFF bytes: the original computes the next store's position, the file size, in 16 bits at cache_save R035+0x1468, so a size of 0x10000 or more wraps to 0 or low), the file is not laid out again. The store the screen is left from is written over its old bytes when it is no longer than they are (a Get only shrinks it, a Put onto an existing entry changes a count; the stale bytes after a shrunk store stay, as in the original's own rewrite, and no offset moves), else nothing is written. Places' handles stay. No offset past 0xFFFF is ever written; Put of a new entry or store is refused (CanPut, Storing.NoRoomMessage). Opened and left without a change, the file is byte-identical.
- **D-444756** `deliberate-fix` - `src/Darklands.Core/Rules/CityPolitics.cs:173` `CityPolitics.SetUpCity`  
  original: `R039+0x0558` (1462:0558, matched)  
  why: `while (!loc_query(loc, d + 3))` loops forever in a city without any shop; here the search stops after seven days.
- **D-553226** `deliberate-fix` - `src/Darklands.Core/Rules/LocationRules.cs:390` `LocationRules.RandomOfType`  
  original: `R039+0x0504` (1462:0504, matched)

- **D-508756** `deliberate-fix` - `src/Darklands.Core/Rules/Storing.cs:54` `Storing.NoRoomMessage`  
  original: `R035+0x0A46` (1462:0A46, matched)
